title: Conditional validity of inductive conformal predictors
relevance: Establishes that split-conformal coverage is guaranteed only MARGINALLY - averaged over calibration draws - and gives the exact Beta distribution of the coverage you actually get from one fixed calibration set. This is the correction our Search 17 note needed: the 1/(n+1) slack describes the average across hypothetical samples, not the single sample we will really collect. Using this we can state, before labelling anything, how far our realized per-year coverage could sit from the nominal target at a chosen n.

title: Conformal prediction: A gentle introduction
source: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 16(4), 494-591
relevance: The standard practitioner reference, and the source of the widely-quoted guidance that a calibration set of roughly 1000 is reasonable - which is about controlling coverage VARIABILITY, not about the validity of the guarantee. Gives us the vocabulary and the defaults for the whole conformal spine, and settles the apparent contradiction between 'valid at any n' and 'you need 1000'. Read together with Vovk 2013 before choosing our per-year sample size.
